translation_en:
…beneath the examination eaves, in the brief time available, it is difficult to enumerate them all. Yet even one such failing would suffice to bring about anomalous portents; how much more so when they are numerous! You gentlemen are concerned for the times and mindful of the state; you revere Heaven’s mandate and pity the people’s distress. Your questions surely express this earnest concern. Yet in my humble view, when we seek the origins of calamities and anomalies, Heaven’s Way is remote and difficult to discern; when we discuss means of dispelling them, human affairs are close at hand and can be set right. In setting human affairs right, what could be more pertinent than the admonitions Yi Yin and Gao Yao gave their rulers? These I have already set forth above.

If one can truly give attention to this, regarding the people as Heaven itself, and regarding Heaven as one’s own heart; fostering reverence and awe, guarding against ease and desire, exercising care in daily conduct, giving due weight to commands, attending to government and restoring its guiding principles, drawing close to the loyal and upright and keeping flatterers at a distance; and, further, lightening labor services and reducing taxes, conserving the people’s strength and cutting expenditure, restraining oneself so that others may have abundance, carrying these measures out with sincerity and maintaining them with firm resolve, persevering without slackening—then one will see the people’s hearts gladdened and Heaven’s disposition turn favorable, calamities and baleful influences disappear, and harmonious vital energy spread everywhere.

This is what Master Dong meant by “Rectify the heart in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify the hundred officials; rectify the hundred officials in order to rectify the myriad people, so that those far and near are all united in rectitude.” It is what Gongsun Hong meant by “When the heart is harmonious, vital energy is harmonious; when vital energy is harmonious, bodily form is harmonious; when bodily form is harmonious, the voice is harmonious; when the voice is harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds.” All objects betokening blessings, and all auspicious signs that can be elicited, will then arrive from every direction. translation_en: …if this is not so, then even if auspicious stars and felicitous clouds daily adorn the heavens, and auspicious qilin and majestic phoenixes daily roam the outlying marshes, what benefit would they bring to good government? Thus, the manifestations of calamities and auspicious signs issue from Heaven, but their root lies in ourselves; the subtle workings of sympathetic response lie in ourselves and do not belong to Heaven. Such is this humble student's view, though its details are not easily expressed. Should you, honored examiners, approve of me and advance me, I may yet have the opportunity to trace the matter from beginning to end and present it below the vermilion steps of the throne.

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

In the second month of spring in the twelfth year of Zhengde [1517], scholars from throughout the realm took the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites. His Majesty commanded your servant Gui, Grand Secretary, to set aside confidential affairs of state and take charge of literary selection; your servant Qing also participated. After the examination compound was sealed, we conducted three sessions and selected 350 men. Their names were listed, and their outstanding compositions were also printed to form a record, to be presented to the throne and circulated throughout the realm. According to established practice, it falls to your servant to write its postface.

Your servant reflects that, at the founding of our dynasty, the sagely progenitor, Emperor Gao, established institutions and laws, entirely sweeping away the habit of excessive formalities of recent ages in order to restore the simple, unadorned governance of the ancient emperors and kings. 九重簡命之盛心且以少裨風化
于萬一而未知其果能否也
抑臣聞之有伯樂而後能別
鹽車之馬有和氏而後能辨
punctuated:
務為新竒，游心高遠，則有淪而入于他岐者矣。夫朝廷者，四方之極也。士之進退，取決于禮闈，又天下之所視以為趨嚮也，而烏敢以弗慎哉？崇雅而去浮，翦華而取實，此有司今日之事，所以仰遵聖祖之貽謀。以為循是而求之，庶乎得所謂誠與才合者，以備將来之實用，以上副九重簡命之盛心，且以少裨風化于萬一，而未知其果能否也。
抑臣聞之，有伯樂而後能别鹽車之馬，有和氏而後能辨
translation_en:
…those who strive for novelty and let their minds wander into lofty abstractions may sink into wayward paths. The court is the pole toward which all quarters turn. Whether scholars advance or are rejected is decided in the examination hall; the whole realm likewise looks to it for direction. How, then, could we dare be anything but circumspect? To esteem refinement and discard superficiality, to prune ornament and select substance: this is the duty of the responsible officials today, and the means by which we reverently follow the guiding legacy of the sagely founder. We believe that, by seeking men according to this principle, we may obtain those in whom, as the saying goes, sincerity and talent are united, ready for practical service in the future. Thus we may fulfill the sovereign’s earnest purpose in selecting and commissioning us, and contribute, however slightly, to moral transformation. Yet we do not know whether we can indeed accomplish this.
Your servant has also heard that only when there is a Bo Le can the worth of a horse hauling a salt cart be recognized, and only when there is a Master He can one discern…

title: 正德十二年會試錄
text:
荆山之璞多士之文冀北之
羣而萬玉之府也要必待具
目而識之而臣非其人也亦
曰盡此心而已矣諸君子之
登名是錄者思
國家之求我與有司之畢力而
搜揚意將以何為也尚相與
===
勉力以圖惟厥終哉
中順大夫詹事府少詹事兼
翰林院學士顧清謹序

===
勉力以圖惟厥終哉
中順大夫詹事府少詹事兼
翰林院學士顧清謹序
punctuated:
荆山之璞。多士之文，冀北之羣而萬玉之府也。要必待具目而識之，而臣非其人也，亦曰盡此心而已矣。諸君子之登名是錄者，思國家之求我與有司之畢力而搜揚，意將以何為也？尚相與勉力以圖惟厥終哉！
中順大夫、詹事府少詹事兼翰林院學士顧清謹序。
translation_en:
…the uncut jade of Mount Jing. The writings of the many candidates are like the herds of northern Ji and a treasury of myriad pieces of jade. They must await someone with a discerning eye to recognize their worth. Your servant is not such a person; I can only say that I have devoted my whole heart to the task.
You gentlemen whose names appear in this record should consider: with what purpose has the state sought us out, and have the responsible officials exerted themselves to discover and advance us? May you encourage one another to strive, keeping in mind how you will carry your endeavors through to the end!
Preface respectfully composed by Gu Qing, Grand Master of Central Compliance, Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
